Title: Lionfish Invasion
Content: Lionfish are native to the Indian and Pacific Oceans. They have recently been found along the southeast coast of the U.S., the Caribbean, and in parts of the Gulf of Mexico. Experts speculate that the lionfish invasion was caused by people dumping unwanted lionfish into the Atlantic Ocean from home aquariums.

Lionfish have venomous spines and feed on small crustaceans and many fish, including the young of important commercial fish species such as snapper and grouper. The current invasion of lionfish most likely started with the dumping of about `12` fish. Today, there are `text(thousands)` of them over a wide area.
